שַׂמְתָּ לִבְּךָ → *considered* fuses verb and noun under rule 30, headed on the verb, with the suffix its own `unrepresented` unit. Rule 30's preference for the whole expression covers the idiom's lexical members; rule 57's 250-unit precedent for a semantically vacuous, unrendered suffix supports keeping it as its own unit rather than inside the fusion. That alternative is the one competing reading here.

Both indefinite articles of *a perfect and an upright man* go to אִישׁ under rule 15, since the noun is what licenses them; the distributive alternative (one to each adjective) is recorded on that unit.
The concessive *although* is on the waw of וַתְּסִיתֵנִי (rule 14's open list); the ASV margin's *Or, that* is a competing connective for the same morpheme, not a different division.
הֲ takes the fronted *Hast* under rule 17, in contrast to the auxiliary-keeps-with-verb readings at 2.9 and 2.10 where no interrogative morpheme stands.
